vocab.notes: The same word for a man or a woman. It declines like an adjective (jarní).
Same for a man or a woman; declines like an adjective: s vedoucím, s vedoucí.
v našem oddělení = in our department

dialogue.setting: Daniel's manager introduces him to the team on his first day.

lines.speaker: Paní Dvořáková
lines.cs: Tak, [[Danieli|Daniel|voc|addressing]], tohle je náš [[tým|tým|nom|naming]]. To je Pavel, náš [[vývojář|vývojář|nom|naming]].
lines.en: So, Daniel, this is our team. This is Pavel, our developer.

lines.speaker: Paní Dvořáková
lines.cs: Tohle je paní Horáková, naše [[účetní|účetní|nom|naming]]. Má na starosti faktury.
lines.en: This is Mrs Horáková, our accountant. She's in charge of invoices.

lines.speaker: Paní Dvořáková
lines.cs: A tohle je Lenka. Pracuje jako [[asistentka|asistentka|nom|after-jako]] a ví úplně všechno.
lines.en: And this is Lenka. She works as an assistant and knows absolutely everything.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.cs: Těší mě. Doufám, že si zapamatuju všechna jména.
lines.en: Nice to meet you. I hope I'll remember all the names.

exercises.listen: Tohle je paní Horáková, naše účetní. Má na starosti faktury.
options: She's the accountant, in charge of invoices
answers: She's the accountant, in charge of invoices

hints.explain: A director would be "ředitelka". "Účetní" is an accountant.
A developer is "vývojář(ka)"; that's Pavel. She's "účetní", the accountant.

exercises.why: "Tohle je paní Horáková, naše účetní. Má na starosti faktury." This is Mrs Horáková, our accountant. She's in charge of invoices.

exercises.prompt: What do we learn about Lenka?
exercises.listen: Pracuje jako asistentka a ví úplně všechno.
options: She's an assistant and knows everything
She's the boss's assistant and is leaving
answers: She's an assistant and knows everything

hints.explain: "Ví úplně všechno" means she knows absolutely everything.

hints.wrong: She's the boss's assistant and is leaving
hints.explain: Nothing about leaving: "pracuje jako asistentka", she works as an assistant.

exercises.why: "Pracuje jako asistentka a ví úplně všechno." She works as an assistant and knows absolutely everything.
pracovat jako + nominative. A woman is a vývojářka.

hints.explain: vývojář is masculine. For a woman: vývojářka.
After jako, use the same case as the subject (nominative): jako vývojářka.

exercises.why: náš is "our" with a masculine noun.

hints.explain: naše is for feminine and neuter nouns. vývojář is masculine: náš vývojář.

exercises.why: mít na starosti + accusative = to be in charge of.
v (in) + locative. Masculine nouns ending in -g, -k, -h, -ch take -u: v marketingu.

hints.explain: After g (and k, h, ch), the masculine locative is -u, not -ě: v marketingu.

exercises.prompt: Welcome! (to one colleague you say ty to)
exercises.why: vítej is the ty form; vítejte is formal or plural.

hints.explain: Vítejte is formal or plural. To one colleague you say ty to: Vítej!

exercises.question: Which case is "asistentka"?
exercises.why: After jako (as), the noun is in the same case as what it describes: here the subject, so the nominative.
Kdo je to? or Kdo to je? Both are natural.

exercises.prompt: Reply politely that you're pleased to meet her too.
exercises.why: Mě taky (likewise), or simply Těší mě back. Dobrý den is the right greeting with a colleague you say vy to.

hints.explain: Paní Horáková greeted you formally (Dobrý den), so answer in kind: Dobrý den, mě taky.
Já taky is "I too". Here it's "(it pleases) me too": Mě taky.
